notes: Form 1040 Line 13b: Schedule 1-A deductions, v2 successor to v1 (P0 Sec. 4: the all-of-Schedule-1-A absence assertion cannot stay once Part V is computed -- a taxpayer with a real, nonzero senior deduction could never truthfully answer the old fact 'yes'). The gate narrows to tax.us.2025.schedule1a.no-parts-ii-iv-deductions-declared (Parts II-IV only: tips, overtime, car loan interest), and the published value becomes the real computed Part V total (tax.us.2025.schedule1a.line37-enhanced-deduction-total) instead of the literal 0 -- v37 is itself a genuine, always-computable amount (0 for a return with no one 65 or older, up to $12,000 for a qualifying joint return), so this rule's own disposition is a real published value whenever it applies, never a stand-in zero. The 'when' guard and its true/false shape are otherwise unchanged from v1: a 'no' answer (the return does have a Parts II-IV deduction, which this milestone still does not compute) leaves the rule inapplicable (guard_inapplicable), exactly as v1's single 'no additional deductions' answer did -- that posture is inherited, not newly decided here, since no case in the contract or plan exercises it differently. An absent answer for either required symbol blocks DEPENDENCY_ABSENT, naming the missing fact, never a silent zero.
